title: Unexpected behavior of "Local to Scene" from 4.6 on scene with Editable Children
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible on 4.6 and 4.7. 
- Not reproducible in 4.5.x

### System information

Godot v4.5.2.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.22042.14002) - AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.11 GiB memory

### Issue description

Possibly relates to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/69424 , https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94919, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/97127

When upgrading our project from 4.5.x to 4.6/4.7, we noticed that the behavior of the "Local to Scene" flag has radically changed on some of our game objects. We have a Local to Scene resource that is referenced in some of our objects as an assigned Override Material. 
On 4.5.x this resource is stored as an external resource in the scene, meaning that changing it will affect all the object that make use of this material. 
When upgrading to 4.6/4.7, the object that was using the resource now stores it as a sub-resource, meaning that now it is impossible to make global changes to all the objects that referenced the material. After discussing this [here](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/general?msg=nQ7D7g4ek7Q8vl3ix) and a massive deep-dive I am coming to the conclusion that this specifically relates to Scenes including meshes set to Editable Children and that it might be a bug introduced with 4.6, so I will re-share some of the information here, hoping that maintainers will help us get closer to a final answer. The support project should make things easier to understand.

I would like to hear from the maintainers if this is a bug in the first place, or if the behavior has changed by design and the information has not been made clear to the user.

First of all, the tooltip of the "Local to Scene" flag reads:

> If `true` the resource is duplicated for each instance of all scenes using it. At run-time the resource can be modified in one scene without affecting other instances (see `PackedScene.instantiate()`).
>Note: Changing this property at run-time has no effect on already created duplicate resources.

I want to focus on "At run-time the resource can be modified in one scene without affecting other instances".

In my opinion this is implying that when NOT at run-time, editing the resource will affect all the objects that reference the resource. As I already mentioned above, this is the behavior on 4.5. It means that All objects using this material still keep a reference to the original material. It is a non-destructive behavior, meaning that I can still edit the material globally, even though at run-time it will be duplicated and I'll be able to edit the material independently from the other objects.

When upgrading to >=4.6, what happens is that

* If "Local To Scene" is false, all objects will still reference the material file.
* If "Local to Scene" is true, all objects will lose the reference to the material file and they will store a sub-resource instead (very destructive behavior, since many of our project objects effectively stop referencing the assigned material). Please note that this happens EXCLUSIVELY in a scene containing a glb set to Editable Children. The reference is set to Local instead. 

To make things a bit more complicated, there definitely is a bug with the Material Override tooltip behavior:
When I have a material with "Local to Scene" true, I drag it on a mesh that is part of an Interited Scene (on 4.5, 4.6 or 4.7), or I drag it on a mesh with Editable Children (4.6 or 4.7), and I hover on the now assigned material, it is showing the original resource (ie `res://my_material.tres`). This suggests that the scene _is_ now referencing the original resource, but behind the scenes Godot has created a sub-resource instead! If I restart the engine, the reference is gone from the tooltip. I think this also contributed to the confusion, since the editor is lying to me about referencing the original resource.

This issue with the tooltip is still a "distraction" from the core topic of how "Local to Scene" actually works. I believe there is a bit of confusion on what "Local to Scene" does and why it can have a very destructive behavior at times.

### Steps to reproduce

* Open project in 4.5
* Create a scene and add a glb file to it
* Set the node as Editable Children
* Create a material, and assign it to the mesh or a submesh as Material Override 
* Notice that it is stored as an external resource reference
* Restart Godot and notice that the reference is still there
* Upgrade the project to 4.6 or 4.7
* See that the reference is now completely lost, and the material now stored as a separate sub-resource instead, making it impossible to edit the material and having it propagate to the mesh.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The project contains

A. Scene with mesh set to Editable Children
B. Inherited Scene with mesh set to Editable Children
C. Scene with mesh set to Local
D. Inherited Scene with mesh set to Local

You will notice that loading the project in 4.5 will keep the reference to the material on both A and C.
When upgrading to 4.6 or 4.6, the reference to the material is only kept on C, while A loses it.

[local-to-scene-(4.5-final).zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30064949/local-to-scene-.4.5-final.zip)
